How engagement is scored

ER = (likes + comments + shares) ÷ followers of the account that posted
  • Own posts: divided by the brand's followers.
  • Creator collabs: divided by the creator's followers, so a 24k creator and a 2M creator compete fairly.
  • Median is reported alongside average, because one viral post can drag an average 3× up.
  • Window: Sept 1 – Nov 10, 2026. 260 posts. Formats tagged reel, carousel, static.

Finding 2 · Format mix

Reels are Barosi's strongest format. Add one text-poster carousel a week

Barosi reels: 0.44% ER, ahead of Rosier (0.25%) and Anveshan (0.16%).

Why not statics? Barosi's static average (0.31%) comes from one Ganesh Chaturthi giveaway (276 comments). Its other statics, the numbered postcards, got 31–52 likes.

Why carousels? Rosier's carousels average 0.38%, its best format. Each opens on a kitchen fear in big type ("This might be making your family sick", 2.3k likes), then gives the fix. People save it and send it to family. Barosi can do the same with proof it already has: "Your ghee should pass this home test", then the test, then Barosi's lab number.

So → keep reels as the core, add one poster carousel a week: a kitchen fear, the fix, Barosi's proof. Recommendation 2

06 · White space

Four ideas no brand in the set is doing

How we found them: all 260 posts from the six brands were checked for each idea. It counts as white space only if no brand posts it and Barosi already has what it needs.

Proof on camera

How we know: 0 of 260 posts show a test result.

Why it works: adulteration is the buyer's top fear. On Barosi's own ghee page a buyer wrote he would buy 3 kg a month if lab reports were shared. Barosi tests milk daily on its Pure & Sure device, so the content already exists.

The morning milk run

How we know: Rosier and Anveshan sell ghee nationally with no own-farm milk in NCR. None of Barosi's 12 brand-made posts shows its milk business.

Why it works: Barosi's milk ads already say "Trusted by 30,000+ families", and milk reaches Gurugram doors by 9 am. Filming the farm-to-door run proves freshness for milk and borrows that trust for ghee.

A winter recipe series

How we know: seasonal dishes were the top food posts (halwa 7.0k shares, laddoo 3.7k), but every one was a one-off creator post.

Why it works: winter is when ghee use peaks, and recipes get saved. A named weekly series makes people come back for the next one.

The founder answers, every fortnight

How we know: Durlabh's festive reel is Barosi's best brand-made post (643 likes), yet he appeared once in 71 days. Anveshan's founders already run a numbered series ("Founders Say").

Why it works: "Who's behind it?" is a top buyer question. One 30–45 second phone video, one real customer question each time ("Why is A2 ghee ₹2,040?"). Low effort for the founder, and it builds trust that compounds.

07 · What peers do well

Six proven moves Barosi can adapt in weeks

Rosier

Education poster carousels

Fear-then-fix posters reach 0.38% ER, Rosier's best format.

Barosi version: "How to spot vanaspati in your ghee", three slides, ends on the bilona process.

Anveshan

A named founder series

"Founders Say, Episode 1" frames the founder as a recurring show.

Barosi version: "Durlabh at the dairy", one honest question a fortnight.

Rosier

Kid and family creators

Niyati (90.3% ER) and twin-skit creators (71.5%) outperform recipe creators 5–10×.

Barosi version: brief "first laddoo made with nani" for winter.

Rosier

The producer as hero

A farmer's face on frame one pulled 62.9k likes (29.8% ER).

Barosi version: the Pataudi gwala team, named, every Sunday.

Rosier

Festival family skits

A Karwa Chauth skit pulled 16.9k likes on a 25.5k-follower creator.

Barosi version: a Lohri skit where the Dolchi is the gift, written in Hinglish.

Barosi already

Founder reels exist

The Diwali founder reel earned 643 likes, well above Barosi's own-post median of 56.

Next step: make it weekly and give it a name.

From Finding 6 · Identity, proof & conversion

One postcard frame, a weekly proof drop, and a CTA that converts

PATAUDI · HRPostcard from Pataudi · Ep 04
FOUNDERDurlabh at the dairy
TESTED ✓Proof drop · Week 47
  • Frame: cream border, dotted stamp corner and brown caption band, taken from the pack. Applied to own posts and requested on creator covers.
  • Proof drop: every Friday, film one Pure & Sure test with the reading on screen. Link the public report page to it.
  • CTA: "Comment GHEE" or "Comment DOODH" triggers an auto-DM with the product link and a first-order code. Bio link goes to a winter collection page.

11 · Website

The website piece: Gurugram homepage, redesigned

Every reel ends in a tap to barosi.in. For this assignment I scoped the website to the Gurugram homepage (barosi.in/local) and redesigned it with Barosi's own products, prices and photos.

A shopper from a reel wants three answers fast: what does it cost, is it real, who makes it. The redesign answers all three on the first scroll.
Today on the siteIn the redesign
PriceTwo clicks to the first priceGrowthPrices on the homepage. Size chips show ₹/L: A2 ghee ₹1,730/L at 500 ml vs ₹1,580/L at 5 L
Milk choiceTwo cards, no monthly costGrowthA "which milk?" picker with monthly cost: A2 at 1 L/day = ₹3,360
ProofIcon tiles; test report link not live yetBrand + Growth6-step farm-to-door photos, a daily test slip, lab result 99.93% milk fat
StoryFounder and Shark Tank not on the homepageBrandMaa and the barosi, Durlabh Rawat, the Shark Tank badge, "Book a farm visit"
BasketSame-ghee multipacks onlyGrowth5 cross-category combos: the duo is a 27% bigger basket than one jar
11 changeseach with why + the number to track0 new photoshoots needed for the first 3
Open the homepage redesign → tap "See what changed & why"
